title: Vesper and the Cover
premise: Paloma Blackwood, a veteran crash investigator haunted by the unexplained loss of his family aboard Flight 4471, has spent seven years buried in bureaucratic anonymity. When a burner phone rings with his dead wife's voice on the line, he is pulled into a conspiracy: a cabal within the aviation safety authority is engineering a mid-air catastrophe timed to the Geneva summit, designed to look like pilot error and bury evidence of their earlier crimes—including row twelve. As Paloma races to decode the voice's cryptic warnings, he discovers his wife may have been an informant whose death was no accident, forcing him to choose between exposing the truth and protecting the last person connected to her. In the end, Paloma thwarts the attack over the Alps at devastating personal cost, testifies against the cabal, and finally opens the go-bag he packed for a life he no longer needs to run from.
about_author: Lena Winterbourne is a former airline safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction to explore what those reports leave unsaid. She lives near a small regional airfield, where she claims the sound of takeoffs helps her think.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Seven years after losing his family on Flight 4471, Paloma works cold cases at the Safety Board, keeping a go-bag by the door and rehearsing his alibi of ordinariness. A routine audit request about 4471 lands on his desk—filed by someone using his wife's maiden name. The beat is dread disguised as routine; grief shown through ritual.

chapters.title: The Burner
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A package arrives containing a burner phone that rings: his wife Vesper's voice, distorted but unmistakable, reciting coordinates and one word—'summit.' He traces the call to a decommissioned relay tower and finds it wiped remotely hours later. Emotional beat: hope curdling into terror as he realizes someone wants him found.

chapters.title: Polished Lie
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, intercut with antagonist Deputy Director Corliss Hale reviewing Paloma's file. Paloma lies to his supervisor about the audit, then breaks into the archive annex and discovers 4471's flight data recorder was swapped before analysis. Beat: the investigator becomes the investigated; paranoia sharpens into purpose.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Static
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The burner calls again; 'Vesper' reveals she left him a trail before she died—a safety deposit key hidden inside the go-bag he's carried for years. Inside: her real identity as a whistleblower who infiltrated the cabal. Beat: love recontextualized—he married a stranger, or thought he had; betrayal and devotion entwined.

chapters.title: Hale's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. We learn the plot: a chartered summit shuttle will be downed over the Alps, blamed on a falsified maintenance record, killing delegates and burying the 4471 evidence chain permanently. Hale identifies Paloma as the loose thread. Beat: chilling competence—the antagonist isn't evil, just efficient; power as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at Dawn
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following Vesper's instructions, he meets her old contact, journalist Amara Osei, who confirms the cabal's reach—and warns that everyone Vesper trusted is dead except her. They trade half-evidences. Beat: reluctant alliance; Paloma realizes staying invisible was always the trap, not the escape.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Hale springs the trap: Paloma is framed for tampering with records, suspended, and hunted. He goes dark, using investigator tradecraft to shadow the summit charter crew and find the sabotaged component already installed. Beat: isolation at its peak—but the hunter's skills finally serve love instead of hiding.

chapters.title: Vesper's Last Recording
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Decoding the final message, he learns the truth: Vesper died buying time to expose the cabal, and the 'voice' is her pre-recorded dead-man's-switch, triggered by Amara when the attack timeline accelerated. Grief arrives whole. Beat: catharsis—she never stopped protecting him; duty and love were the same thing to her.

chapters.title: Forty-Seven Minutes
chapters.summary: Paloma and Amara's POV alternating. The climax: they must convince air traffic control and ground the charter before it crosses the Alps, while Hale triggers a lockdown and sends enforcers. Paloma broadcasts the falsified maintenance data mid-flight, forcing an emergency diversion; Hale is arrested as the plane lands short of its kill zone. Beat: breathless, kinetic, earned.

chapters.title: What the Go-Bag Was For
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue months later. Testimony concluded, the cabal dismantled, Paloma unpacks the go-bag at last: inside, beside Vesper's key, he leaves a new item—a boarding pass, seat 12A, for a flight he chooses to take. Beat: quiet resolution; memory honored, duty fulfilled, love carried forward instead of mourned.
